text:
anya: Heads-up — seeing an ~18% p50 latency regression on mistral-mqa after the kernel-selector patch rolled to stable. Regression triggers when seq > 1024 and KV cache hit rate is high.

phil: link to dashboard? which commit was rolled? :thinking:

anya: dashboard: https://redwood.internal/perf/1841  commit c3f5b2e (kernel-hint-opt). Last good at 1839. Quick numbers: p50 24ms -> 28.4ms, p95 120ms -> 155ms.

jamal: Ran a micro-profile on g4-16 last night. Short flame:
```text
kv_copy_async       34%
kernel_dispatch     22%
attention_kernel    18%
python_overhead     6%
```
Looks like extra KV copying and dispatch overhead after the selector change.

mira: Is this limited to GQA or also MQA? Any RoPE-scale changes recently? If head dim/layout assumptions changed, paged KV can get fragmentation and extra memcpy.

kai: repro script I used: 
```bash
./bench.sh --model=mistral-8x --seq=2048 --batch=8 --kv-paged --num_kv_heads=32 --kv_dim=64
```
Repro is stable on my node.

jamal: Interesting: when I flip `num_key_value_heads` to 16, throughput improves ~12% and `kv_copy_async` drops considerably. Suggests stride/alignment issue — head boundary crossing triggers non-vectorized copies.

anya: Also observed a surge in small allocations and slab fragmentation in paged-KV when heads != physical warp layout. Heap trace shows many ~256B allocs at steady state.

perf-bot: deploy event: kernel-hint-opt rolled to stable at 2024-11-03T15:22Z (build c3f5b2e) :arrow_up_small:

phil: Can we run a kernel variant that forces aligned head packing and compare? The selector may be choosing a different attention kernel for long sequences.

mira: Agreed. Also verify RoPE scaling interactions — mixtral uses 64-dim heads, qwen uses 128; code paths that assume uniform head dims can produce interleaved paged layouts. Proposed quick plan:
- Run bench with `--kv_layout=packed_heads` vs `--kv_layout=per_head_stride`
- Compare `--force_kernel=attn_v2` vs `attn_v1`
- Sweep `num_key_value_heads` 8/16/32

anya: I'll queue those experiments now and post raw logs. Also starting a canary rollback to previous kernel selector for the next 30m.

jamal: Note: a short-term hack (aligning `kv_slot` to 512B) reduced memcpy count and improved p50 by ~8%, but increases memory by ~1.5%. Could be an acceptable mitigation while we root-cause.

kai: Small additional data point: batcher heuristics were changed last week to favor larger batches when seq > 1024. That increased effective batch size in the window where misaligned copies are worst — so the two changes likely amplified the tail.

phil: Ok owners: jamal + anya triage infra + KV; mira handle attention/kernel side; kai check batching heuristics. I'll open a ticket and add perf traces. :+1:

anya: Adding logs now — will update thread with bench filenames and flamegraph links.

jamal: If anyone has time, please run a quick check on a dedicated node with `--kv_layout=packed_heads` so we can decide rollback vs mitigation.

mira: I can try `attn_v2` variant in a couple hours and report back.

phil: Thanks team — keep this thread for updates.
